name: alert
description: A short message that needs attention: status, success, warning, or error. Not for long content.

use.when: something needs attention now: a failure, a warning before an action, or a result the person waited for.
use.not: content that stays on the page, a heading, or anything a person did not need to be interrupted for.
use.with: a status region for what changes over time; text for anything longer than two sentences.

title.description: Optional short title, a heading before the message.

level.title: Heading level
level.description: Where the title sits in the page outline.

live.description: Announce it: for a message put on the page after it loaded, or an action's outcome. A message present when the page loads is not announced whatever its role.

icon.description: A mark to show instead of the kind's own (ℹ, ✓, ⚠, or a circled ! for an error). Hidden from screen readers, which hear the kind as a word.

dismiss.description: When true, renders a close button with data-dismiss attribute.

a11y.role: paragraphs under a heading when titled; with live, status for info and success and alert for warning and danger

keyboard.does: Focuses the close button when present.
Activates the close button, dismissing the alert.

wcag.notes: Kind is said as a word read first, a mark of its own shape, an edge and a tint, never colour alone (1.4.1); in forced colours a warning or error edge turns double. A title is a heading (1.3.1, 2.4.6). Only a live alert takes role=alert or status, since a message present on load is not announced (4.1.3). The close button is a whole 44px target (2.5.5) and never covers the words.

machine.identify: Read data-kind for the severity and the text content for the message.
machine.operate: Read it before retrying; a dismissible one has a Close message button.
